newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen extending surge next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen extending surge next week.

text.p: The Polish bourse is seen extending its 36.8-percent, two-month surge next week, as foreign investors seem ready to continue their buying frenzy despite ever rising prices, analysts said.

"It seems to me that next week can be very similar to this though for about two weeks there has been no fundamental reason for that to happen," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria Securities.
Analysts said the bourse could keep rising along with major Western exchanges, also enjoying bull runs.
The main WIG index rose 4.1 percent this week to 18,177.2 points, setting its third straight 34-month high on Friday.
But some analysts said growth could slow significantly next week, or that even a downward correction could hit, as investors finally take profits.
"Prices are at such a level that some investors will start to take profits," said Maciej Matusiak of PKO BP brokerage.
Analysts said investors would be watching the bulk of firms' January earnings reports to be released early next week.

They said two of the main market's top gainers this week, Budimex up 34.8 percent and Elektromontaz Export up 23.5 percent, could be gaining in anticipation of good earnings data during this year's warm January.
Analysts said Budimex was also buoyed by the domestic demand that followed the foreign buying reflected by Societe Generale's announcement it had more than five percent of the builder.

They said Optimus, up 30.9 percent, continued to be buoyed by last week's news it had received orders to convert 159 of its convertible bonds, freeing reserves linked with the issue and raising January pre-tax profit by 1.3 million zlotys.
Analysts said the current strong market would likely not be affected by January inflation data due on Monday, especially as no near-term interest-rare change was expected.
They said the Peasant Party's withdrawal of support for its agriculture minister Roman Jagielinski could only hurt the bourse in the unlikely event the ruling coalition collapsed.

They said the market was also likely strong enough to keep rising despite the finance ministry's Thursday decision to free fuel prices, seen adding up to one point to the government's 1997 year-on-year inflation target of 13 percent.
Garment maker Elpo SA on Thursday becomes the first stock to trade on the bourse's new third floor of especially small, less-liquid stocks.
On Friday Amerbank transfers to the main market from the parallel floor.
